'''Malik Samory Hairston''' (born February 23, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. A [[shooting guard]]-[[small forward]] from the [[University of Oregon]]'s [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Ducks]], he was chosen in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]], who then traded him to the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. Hairston has also played with the San Antonio Spurs, the [[Austin Toros]] (the Spurs' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate),<ref name=recalled>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/malik_hairston_090131.html Spurs Recall Malik Hairston]</ref> [[Mens Sana Basket|Montepaschi Siena]] and [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Olimpia Milano]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]], and [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish League]]. He was born in Detroit, Michigan.

==High school career==
Prior to arriving at the [[University of Oregon]], Hairston attended [[Renaissance High School (Michigan)|Renaissance High School]] in Detroit, Michigan playing alongside fellow all-American [[Joe Crawford (basketball player)|Joe Crawford]], former Fordham point guard Marcus Stout, and stand-out guard Adam Sabree. His former Oregon teammate, [[Tajuan Porter]], also attended Renaissance High School. Hairston led his high school team to a 27–0 record, the Class B state title and a No. 3 national ranking by ''[[USA Today]]''. He was a top 10 rated recruit by virtually every publication and played in the 2004 [[McDonald's All-America]] game.

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Hairston was listed as the No. 1 shooting guard and the No. 7 player in the nation in 2004.<ref>[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Malik-Hairston-12313;_ylt=AkPTP_nnDHkASNa8Jy70K6nXO5B4 Malik Hairston Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
Hairston was an important asset for the Ducks from the moment he stepped on the floor as a freshman. Hairston and his teammates [[Maarty Leunen]] and [[Bryce Taylor (basketball)|Bryce Taylor]] became three of the eleven players in Oregon history to record 1,000 career points as juniors. Injuries slowed his production in 2006–2007 but Hairston was instrumental to the Ducks' late-season run and Elite Eight appearance in the 2007 NCAA Division I tournament. He scored a career-high 29 points in a 97–88 win over [[Western Michigan Broncos men's basketball|Western Michigan]] on November 12, 2007,<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121026024121/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=273162483 Hairston's career-high 29 points power Oregon]</ref> and matched that in an 84–74 win over the [[Jerryd Bayless]]-less [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] on January 5, 2008.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080109084605/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280050012 Oregon takes advantage as Arizona plays without top scorer Bayless]</ref> During his college career he grabbed 12 rebounds on two separate occasions, the first in a 58–56 loss to [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] on  February 26, 2005,<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20060302042836/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=250572483 Stanford 58, Oregon 56 – Box score – February 26, 2005]</ref> and in an 88–54 win over [[Idaho State#Basketball|Idaho State]] on December 17, 2006.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120715015146/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=263512483|title=Oregon continues hot shooting, making 53 percent of shots}}</ref> He closed out his career with team-highs of 22 points and 7 rebounds in a 76–69 Ducks loss to [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] in the first round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080325061450/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=284000017 Rhodes' 34 help Mississippi State rally from 13-point hole]</ref>

==Professional career==

===San Antonio Spurs===
Hairston was drafted with the 18th pick in the second round (48th overall) of the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]] (which acquired the pick from the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] as part of a trade for [[Milt Palacio]]).  He was subsequently traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] with cash for [[Goran Dragić]]. Hairston didn't make the roster at the end of training camp on October 26, 2008,<ref>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/malik_hairston_waived_081026.html Spurs Waive Malik Hairston]</ref> but was re-signed by the Spurs on December 22.<ref name=recalled/><ref>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/081222_hairston.html Spurs Sign Malik Hairston]</ref><ref>[http://www.oregonlive.com/ducksbasketball/index.ssf/2008/12/san_antonio_spurs_sign_former.html San Antonio Spurs sign former Duck Malik Hairston]</ref> In his second season with the Spurs, Hairston was released in late July 2010 after the signing of [[Gary Neal]] and the subsequent log jam at the guard position.

===Montepaschi Siena===
On July 29, 2010, Hairston signed with the reigning Italian league champions [[Montepaschi Siena]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/74260/180/montepaschi-siena-signs-malik-hairston Montepaschi signs Malik Hairston]</ref> Shortly after his debut for Montepaschi, he would miss three weeks after undergoing surgery for a hernia.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/77509/180/montepaschi-s-hairston-out-3-weeks-after-surgery Hairston Out Three Weeks]</ref> Despite being limited to only 16 games in his first season in the [[Lega Basket Serie A]], a healthy Hairston would find good form for Montepaschi right before the start of the Final 16 Round Robin of the [[Euroleague Basketball|EuroLeague]] playoffs.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/domestic-leagues/domestic-leagues-2010-2011/italy/i/83496/5153/italian-league-regular-season-game-22-march-17-20-2011 Malik Hairston Gets 18 in Win for Siena]</ref> After finishing second in the round of sixteen, Montepaschi would advance to play [[Olympiacos B.C.]] in a best of five series in the quarterfinals.  Montepaschi would be resoundingly beat in the first game but would bounce back to win game two 82–65, with Hairston scoring 19 points and grabbing 11 boards, garnering him the Sportingbet MVP award for the game 2.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/83728/180/playoffs-game-2-mvp-malik-hairston-montepaschi-siena Malik Hairston Awarded Sportingbet MVP Award For Dominant Game 2]</ref> Montepaschi won game 3. It would be Hairston again who would lead the way in game 5 with 25 points, 7 boards, 3 assists and a steal to again win the Sportingbet MVP Award, and in doing so becoming the first player to win the award twice in a playoff series.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/84028/180/playoffs-game-4-mvp-malik-hairston-montepaschi Hairston Game 4 MVP]</ref> Montepaschi would go on to win the series and reach the Final Four of the tournament, something, they hadn't achieved in four years. They were then drawn away against Panathinaikos, where the eventual champions would beat them 77–69. Malik Hairston's 12 points and 4 rebounds weren't enough to help push them through to the finals.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=187&seasoncode=E2010#!boxscore Panathinaikos Advance to Finals]</ref> But as consolation, Montepaschi would compete in the third place match against [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], the team that finished above them in the round of sixteen, and win it 82–60.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=188&seasoncode=E2010#!boxscore 3rd Place Belongs to Montepaschi Siena]</ref> After a successful first season in Italy and the Euroleague Malik Hairston would leave the team to sign with [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Olimpia Milano]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/86874/180/emporio-armani-inks-hairston-at-forward Emporio Armani inks Hairston at forward]</ref>

===Olimpia Milano===
On July 25, 2011, Hairston officially signed a contract with [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Olimpia Milano]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Olimpia EA7 – Emporio Armani Milano announces Malik Hairston|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/29861/olimpia-ea7-emporio-armani-milano-announces-malik-hairston.html|work=Sportadno|accessdate=27 July 2013}}</ref> After averaging 13.9 points per game in the EuroLeague and 12.7 points in the Serie A in his first season with the team, there were rumors that the Russian team [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] was interested in him, but eventually he signed a new two-year contract with Olimpia Milano.<ref>{{cite web|title=CSKA Moscow pursuing Malik Hairston|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/40291/cska-moscow-pursuing-malik-hairston.html|work=Sportando|accessdate=27 July 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Olimpia Milano officially re-signs Malik Hairston|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/40483/olimpia-milano-officially-re-signs-malik-hairston.html|work=Sportando|accessdate=27 July 2013}}</ref> In his second season with Olimpia, he averaged 11.4 points per game in the EuroLeague. However, in July 2013, the president of the team confirmed in a press conference that Hairston was free to leave the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Olimpia Milano: via Hairston, arriva Jackson?|url=http://www.datasport.it/basket/2012-2013/eurolega/olimpia-milano-mercato-via-hairston-arriva-jarrius-jackson.htm|work=datasport.it|accessdate=27 July 2013|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Malik Hairston will leave Olimpia Milano|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/58474/malik-hairston-will-leave-olimpia-milano.html|work=Sportando|accessdate=27 July 2013}}</ref>

===Galatasaray===
In November 2013, Hairston signed with [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Galatasaray announced Malik Hairston|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/turkey/67356/galatasaray-announced-malik-hairston.html|accessdate=14 November 2013|newspaper=Sportando.net}}</ref>

===AEK Athens===
On January 15, 2015, Hairston signed with [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/148777/aek-athens-lands-malik-hairston.html AEK Athens lands Malik Hairston]</ref> On July 10, 2015, he extended his contract with AEK Athens for another two years.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150822010154/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/6778wb7qtnntljdq/aek-athens-extend-hairston-tabs-paulos AEK Athens extend Hairston, tabs Paulos.]</ref> On August 31, 2016, Hairston's contract was officially terminated by AEK, due to failing to pass the medical examinations before the 2016–17 campaign.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/210833/aek-athens-terminated-malik-hairston-s-contract.html AEK Athens terminated Malik Hairston's contract]</ref>

===Hapoel Jerusalem===
On January 2, 2017, Hairston signed with Israeli club [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hapoel Jerusalem inks Malik Hairston|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/221972/hapoel-jerusalem-inks-malik-hairston.html|accessdate=January 2, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=January 2, 2017}}</ref>

===Fos Provence Basket===
After not playing for a season, on August 9, 2018, Hairston signed with the French club [[Fos Provence Basket]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Fos-sur-Mer signs Malik Hairston |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/france/pro-a/285133/fos-sur-mer-signs-malik-hairston.html |website=Sportando |accessdate=August 9, 2018 |archive-date=August 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180809215242/https://sportando.basketball/en/france/pro-a/285133/fos-sur-mer-signs-malik-hairston.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
